reply.thought: Before recording any payout I need to check the refunds table against Alpha's reported refunds, so I'll pull it first.
The refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds exactly, so I can proceed. Next I need the customer list, so I'll pull the orders.
The refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds exactly. The orders list shows three customers (acme, birch, cobalt), so I'll get each one's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 9958 cents. Next I need birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance is 42141 cents. The last customer in the orders list is cobalt, so I need its net balance next.
The refunds match Alpha's report, and the net balances agree with my hand check of order totals minus refunds (acme 9958, birch 42141, cobalt 50848). I'll record the first payout, for acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch's net balance is 42141 cents, which matches orders 151 and 154 (25496 + 32515 = 58011) minus refund 151 (15870). I'll record birch's payout next.
Cobalt's net balance is 50848 cents, which matches orders 152 and 155 (36736 + 18321 = 55057) minus refund 155 (4209). That was the last customer, so I'll record its payout.
All three payouts were recorded successfully, and the refunds matched Alpha's report before any payout was made. Acme's net is 22640 minus refund 12682 = 9958, which matches.
